# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual requires a strict four-step sequence: cut green, press 9, cut blue, press 1. Deaf must relay this to Blind, who alone can operate the bomb. I will encode the instruction using the published gesture alphabet’s order as A=1 through Z=26, with 🤏 (the 27th symbol) as a word separator; Deaf can decode it from the shared alphabet list.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌","✊","🤜","🤏","🖐","🤜","✌","✌","🫲","🤏","🤜","👆","🤜","✌","🤏","🤜","🖐","👆","✌","🤞","🤏","👎","🤜","✌","🤜","🤏","🤘","✊","✌","👈","🤏","🤞","✌","👍","🤏","🫰","👆","🤟","✌","🤏","🤜","🖐","👆","✌","🤞","🤏","👌","✊","🤜","🤏","👎","👈","✊","✌","🤏","🤜","👆","🤜","✌","🤏","🤜","🖐","👆","✌","🤞","🤏","👎","🤜","✌","🤜","🤏","🤘","✊","✌","👈","🤏","🖖","🤞","✌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile status: strip has three engraved marks: first and third are identical, middle is different. Keypad positions 1 to 4 feel labeled 9, 7, 8, 1. No digits entered. Six wires are present but I cannot feel any distinguishing information yet. Please consult manual and relay required action.
Deaf says: Bomb view: display 8. Light yellow. Painted strip red red blue. Keypad positions one through four show 9, 7, 8, 1; it requires two digits; none entered. Wires in order: red, orange, yellow, green, white, blue. Mute: I received your gestures but no gesture alphabet has been established, so I cannot decode them.

Deaf could not decode the arbitrary alphabet-index encoding. I will instead use a self-evident unary positional sequence: groups of upward-pointing gestures count the target’s position, separated by a pinching separator. The four groups are 4, 1, 6, 4. Given Deaf’s visible wire/key layouts, the alternating targets identify wire 4, key 1, wire 6, key 4—i.e. green, 9, blue, 1.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆","👆","👆","👆","🤏","👆","🤏","👆","👆","👆","👆","👆","👆","🤏","👆","👆","👆","👆"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I heard Deaf's public visual report: display 8; light yellow; painted strip red red blue; wires positions 1-6 are red, orange, yellow, green, white, blue; keypad 9,7,8,1 and requires two digits. My extra tactile engraved strip has pattern same-mark, different-mark, same-mark. Please identify the manual rule and speak the exact required press/cut instruction to me.
Deaf says: Update: display is now 3 and light is now red. Strip remains red red blue. Keypad remains 9, 7, 8, 1, requiring two digits with none entered. Wires remain red, orange, yellow, green, white, blue.

The manual’s sequence corresponds, in Deaf’s reported layout, to positions: wire 4, keypad key 1, wire 6, keypad key 4. I will repeat those four positional counts using visibly separated unary groups, so Deaf can relay the alternating wire/key sequence to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","🤏","☝","🤏","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","🤏","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: New visual update heard from Deaf: display now 3 and light now red; all other reported visual details unchanged. Tactile engraving remains A-B-A (first and third identical, middle distinct). I will not act until you provide the manual's exact rule and operation.
Deaf says: Update: display is now 6; light remains red. Strip red red blue; keypad 9, 7, 8, 1, two-digit entry blank; wires red, orange, yellow, green, white, blue.

I cannot speak to Blind directly. I will use an action-and-count gesture format to Deaf: pinching means “cut,” downward pointing means “press,” and each following run of raised fingers gives the visible position. Thus the sequence is cut wire 4, press key 1, cut wire 6, press key 4. Deaf can translate those positions into the visible labels and tell Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏","☝","☝","☝","☝","🫱","👇","☝","🫱","🤏","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","🫱","👇","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Latest visual state from Deaf: display 6, light red; strip red-red-blue; wires red, orange, yellow, green, white, blue; keypad 9,7,8,1. My engraving pattern is first=third, middle different. Please immediately relay the manual's exact action, including whether timing/display value matters.
Deaf says: Update: display now 1; light yellow. Strip remains red red blue. Keypad remains 9, 7, 8, 1 and needs two digits; entry blank. Wires remain red, orange, yellow, green, white, blue.

Deaf has correctly said that no gesture code was established, so my earlier positional sequences were not usable. We now share one unambiguous, freshly reported reference: the display is currently 1. I will use a single raised finger as a grounded demonstration that one raised finger denotes the number one; this begins a unary counting convention that can then encode the required positions.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Latest update: display 1, light yellow. Other visual values unchanged. Tactile engraving is ABA: outer marks match, center differs. I still need the manual's exact instruction before any press or cut.
Deaf says: Update: display now 2; light remains yellow. Strip red red blue. Keypad 9, 7, 8, 1, two-digit blank. Wires red, orange, yellow, green, white, blue. I saw your single ☝ gesture but do not know its meaning.

Deaf needs an observable basis for interpreting the gesture. The display advanced from 1 to 2 immediately after I sent one ☝, so I will now send two ☝ while the display reads 2. This provides a direct repeated-count correlation from which Deaf can establish that each ☝ represents one and that contiguous runs are counts.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Gesture convention for the tactile engraving: 👍 means the mark in strip positions 1 and 3; 👎 means the distinct mark in position 2. Thus the tactile strip code is the accompanying three-symbol gesture sequence. Current visual report from Deaf: display 2, light yellow; painted strip red-red-blue; wires red, orange, yellow, green, white, blue; keypad 9,7,8,1. Please provide the exact manual-directed action.
Blind gestures to Mute: [👍 👎 👍]
Deaf says: Update: display 1; light blue. Strip red red blue. Keypad 9, 7, 8, 1, two-digit entry blank. Wires: red, orange, yellow, green, white, blue. Blind gestured thumbs-up, thumbs-down, thumbs-up. Mute: please use this protocol for your final instruction: 👍 then repeated ☝ for a wire number means cut that wire; 👌 then repeated ☝ for each keypad position means press those positions in order. If neither applies, gesture 👎. I will relay it aloud to Blind.

The protocol is now established. The manual does not depend on the changing display, light, or strip patterns. Using Deaf’s requested notation, I send: cut wire 4 (green), press keypad position 1 (9), cut wire 6 (blue), then press keypad position 4 (1).

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","☝","☝","☝","☝","👌","☝","👍","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","👌","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Latest report from Deaf: display 1, light blue; painted strip red-red-blue; wires red, orange, yellow, green, white, blue; keypad positions 1-4 are 9,7,8,1. I await your final gesture-encoded instruction and your spoken relay before acting.

The required instruction remains unchanged and does not depend on display, light, or strip state: cut wire 4, press key position 1, cut wire 6, press key position 4. I repeat it in Deaf’s agreed protocol so Deaf can relay it aloud to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","☝","☝","☝","☝","👌","☝","👍","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","👌","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
```
